0: Actinic keratoses: rough, scaly, hyperkeratotic patch on sun-damaged skin with erythematous base and dotted vessels — precancerous lesion on sun-exposed sites.
1: Basal cell carcinoma: pearly translucent papule with arborizing vessels, leaf-like areas, blue-grey ovoid nests, and shiny white structures — locally invasive skin malignancy.
2: Benign keratosis: stuck-on seborrheic keratosis with cerebriform surface, milia-like cysts, comedo-like openings, well-demarcated borders, and waxy brown-to-black pigmentation.
3: Dermatofibroma: central white scar-like patch surrounded by delicate peripheral pigment network — firm benign dermal papule with positive dimple sign.
4: Melanoma: asymmetric lesion with atypical pigment network, blue-white veil, regression structures, irregular streaks, and multiple colours — malignant melanocytic tumour meeting ABCDE criteria.
5: Melanocytic nevi: benign symmetric mole with regular pigment network, uniform brown-to-black colour, smooth borders, and homogeneous or globular pattern.
6: Vascular lesion: cherry angioma or pyogenic granuloma with well-defined red to purple lacunae, reddish homogeneous area, sharp borders, and no pigment network.
